chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ali al-Asadi narrated to us: He said: Roqaya bint Ishaq ibn Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them all) narrated to me: My father Ishaq ibn Musa ibn Ja'far narrated to me, from his father Musa ibn Ja'far, from his father Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father, from the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:

A servant's feet will not move on the Day of Resurrection until he is asked about four things: about his life, how he spent it; and about his youth, what he used it for; and about his wealth, from where he earned it and in what he spent it; and about our love, the People of the House.

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ: the People of the House (Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: What are the four things a person is asked about on the Day of Judgment according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Khisal* through an unbroken chain to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, this hadith highlights the four pillars of accountability on the Day of Judgment. It uniquely emphasizes 'love for the Ahl al-Bayt' as a distinct criterion alongside the management of time, youth, and wealth, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *wilayah* as integral to faith. This narration serves as a practical framework for self-assessment, linking spiritual devotion with ethical stewardship of one's life resources.
